Testing a neighborhood rain gauge

I installed a simple rain gauge beside the community garden to compare our measurements with the weather station across town. The first week taught us that placement matters more than the price of the instrument. Nearby leaves can shelter the opening and change the amount of water we record.

Observations

A consistent schedule helped us compare readings after each shower. We emptied the container at the same time every morning and wrote down any unusual conditions. The notebook also records who took the reading, so an unexpected result can be checked against the original observation.

Our next experiment will use a second gauge in an open part of the garden. We will keep both instruments in place for a month, compare the totals, and publish the measurements with notes about wind and nearby plants. The experiment is small, but neighbors can repeat it without specialist equipment.
